artists.biography:
Screaming Trees was an American rock band formed in Ellensburg, Washington in 1985 by vocalist Mark Lanegan, guitarist Gary Lee Conner, bass player Van Conner and drummer Mark Pickerel. Pickerel had been replaced by Barrett Martin by the time the band reached its most successful period. Although widely associated with grunge, the band's sound incorporated hard rock and psychedelic elements. Since its formation, Screaming Trees released seven studio albums, five EPs and three compilations.

Screaming Trees is known as one of the "Godfathers of Grunge" along with the Melvins, U-Men, Skin Yard, Soundgarden, Green River, Cosmic Psychos and Malfunkshun. Screaming Trees rose to fame as part of the grunge movement of the early 1990s, along with bands such as Alice in Chains, Stone Temple Pilots, Pearl Jam, Nirvana and Soundgarden and was one of the most successful underground music acts of the 1990s. The band achieved one top ten single on the Modern Rock Tracks charts. Screaming Trees were plagued by extended inactivity due to their problems with making a follow up to Dust. This led to their official breakup in 2000.

perplexity.description:
Sweet Oblivion is the sixth studio album by American rock band Screaming Trees, originally released on September 8, 1992, through Epic Records. The album is a defining work in the band’s discography, marking their commercial peak and their closest approach to mainstream success. Musically, Sweet Oblivion blends alternative rock, grunge, and neo-psychedelia, characterized by Mark Lanegan’s deep, haunting vocals, Gary Lee Conner’s layered guitar work, and the rhythm section’s dynamic drive. The production, led by Don Fleming, gives the album a polished yet gritty sound that captures the essence of the early 1990s Seattle rock scene.

The album’s standout track, “Nearly Lost You,” became the band’s biggest hit, gaining widespread exposure after its inclusion on the Singles: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack. This exposure helped Sweet Oblivion sell over 300,000 copies, making it the band’s best-selling record. The album was also notable for being the first to feature drummer Barrett Martin, who replaced founding member Mark Pickerel. Critically, Sweet Oblivion was praised for its songwriting and atmospheric depth, solidifying Screaming Trees’ reputation as one of the more distinctive acts in the alternative rock landscape of the era.
